outlook.statement: The Company remains committed to identifying and pursuing opportunities that align with its strategic objectives while maintaining financial discipline and effective risk management practices. We will continue to focus on strengthening our business operations, enhancing efficiency, and exploring opportunities that complement our existing business segments. Our emphasis remains on sustainable growth, prudent capital allocation, operational excellence, and delivering consistent value to all stakeholders. We believe that our strong financial position, experienced leadership, and disciplined approach will enable us to capitalize on emerging opportunities and navigate future challenges successfully.
Outlook of the business has been discussed in detail in the Management Discussion and Analysis which forms part of this Annual Report.

The PVC Engineering Sheets segment is expected to witness steady growth, driven by increasing demand from infrastructure, environmental, and affordable housing projects. Continued investments in sewage and water treatment systems and favorable market conditions are expected to support demand for PVC sheets.

risks: The Company has in place a mechanism to identify, assess, evaluate, monitor and mitigate various risks to key business objectives. Major risks identified by the businesses and functions are systematically addressed through mitigating actions on a continuing basis.
Commodity price risk due to fluctuations in commodity prices driven by external market forces
Raw material price volatility (linked to crude oil)
Strict environmental regulations and plastic bans
Import competition from low-cost foreign manufacturers
Capital-intensive upgrades needed for compliance and competitiveness
Overcapacity in plastic sheet industry leading to under-utilization of resources
Competition, price realization, forex market, changes in government policies and regulations, tax regimes, economic development

Credit risk from cash and cash equivalents, financial assets carried at amortised cost, deposits with banks and financial institutions, and credit exposures to customers including outstanding receivables
Liquidity risk - risk that the Company will not be able to meet its financial obligations as they become due
Market risk comprising foreign currency risk, interest rate risk, and other price risk such as commodity risk
Foreign currency risk primarily relates to import of goods
Interest rate risk - Company primarily borrows under fixed interest rate arrangements
Price risk - Company not significantly exposed to changes in prices of commodities/equity instruments
